slice 4 writer design: two passes because manifest.json is first and states every stored length. Plan pass writes nothing: raw assets cost only open() (declared len = stored len, bounded by max_entry_bytes), a zstd/shuffle_zstd asset is read, hashed and encoded once (one blob), keeping only (codec, stored len, raw_len, elem_size); all structural checks (names, limits, manifest size, entry count, totals, previews) run here so they write no byte. Write pass: manifest, document, rest by name exactly as write_package_with; raw assets copy through one reusable 1 MiB chunk with SHA-256 and CRC-32 running, local header written with CRC 0 and the 4-byte CRC field patched by seek afterwards (no data descriptors: canonical-form reader unchanged); codec assets are read and encoded again (deterministic) and must reproduce the planned codec and length. ZipWriter gained begin_streamed/write_streamed/end_streamed (add and the header builder were refactored onto shared admit/local_header; output unchanged)

slice 4 verification: SHA-256 against the requested digest and length against the declared len are checked while streaming (hash_mismatch / length_mismatch, existing error codes; no new variants); save_atomic_streaming then flush + sync_all, compares file length with the receipt, reopens the temp and runs PackageReader::open + verify_all (structure, every CRC, manifest, every entry SHA-256, document id and revision) before the atomic replace; any failure removes only the temp and marker and leaves the last-good destination byte-identical

decisions: Streaming save is a second, additive path (AssetStream / write_package_streaming / save_atomic_streaming), the buffered AssetSource / write_package_with / save_atomic stay for in-memory callers and checkpoints

Local-header CRC is patched by seek (Write+Seek sink) instead of data descriptors or a pre-pass over the data: the canonical-form reader forbids descriptors and a pre-pass would read every raw asset twice

Codec assets are read twice (plan + write) because manifest.json comes first and needs the stored length; encoding is deterministic and the second encode must reproduce codec and length or the save fails with length_mismatch; raw assets are read once
In-house STORE-only ZIP64 + crc32fast (lead decision); no mimetype entry; ASCII names; archive comments, trailing bytes, non-ZIP64 extra fields rejected
Blob table = optional per-entry fields (codec, raw_len, elem_size, preview) in the manifest, container_version stays 1, one canonical form
Shuffle selection is automatic per blob from the tile format name; unknown format names or conflicting formats for one digest fall back to plain zstd
Previews are derived data: re-saving an Opened without supplying previews drops them; they are not quarantined
Aggregate decoded bound counts previews too (conservative, although read_package never decodes them)
StdFs is not a unit struct (holds owner locks): StdFs::new()
known_gaps: streaming save: a codec (zstd/shuffle_zstd) asset is read and encoded twice per save (CPU 2x for those blobs) and transiently costs ~3-4x its size plus encoder state (measured ~7 MiB for a 1 MiB blob; not measured near max_entry_bytes); only raw assets are strictly one-chunk

streaming save: no in-memory pre-verification of the finished package (there is none); verification is the on-disk re-read (CRC, manifest, every SHA-256) before the rename, which buffers one decoded blob for shuffle_zstd entries; the generic write_package_streaming leaves a partial archive in the sink on a content fault, only the save_atomic_streaming wrapper is all-or-nothing

streaming save: previews and preserved entries come from caller-resident slices and compressed preview copies are held for the duration of the write; the AssetStream must return the same bytes on every open and the writer has one reader open at a time

Oracle independence for the container itself: own writer vs own reader; mitigated by Python zipfile acceptance, an independent raw ZIP builder in tests, and libzstd as independent encoder/decoder for zstd
ruzstd encoder verified at CompressionLevel::Fastest only; it compresses shuffled floats far worse than libzstd (31504 B vs 2693 B on the linear gradient)
Shuffle decode buffers the whole decoded blob (bounded by max_entry_bytes and the aggregate bound) because un-shuffling needs every plane

kill during the rename call itself not covered; Windows power-loss durability of the rename not provable through std (documented in DESCRIPTOR); unix parent-dir fsync failure ignored; lock-based sweep unverified on network filesystems
ReadOnly folio inspections cannot be re-written; Opened materialises all non-preview entries (bounded by limits), use PackageReader::read_asset for lazy access
